concept: MongoDB Compound Index Design: ESR, Selectivity, Covering and Multikey Bounds
summary: A compound index stores references ordered by several fields; key order (equality fields first, then sort, then range — the ESR guideline), selectivity, prefix rules, covered queries, multikey index bounds with $elemMatch and partial/sparse filter semantics decide whether a query can use the index and how many keys and documents it examines. Compiled from MongoDB manual and Atlas pages plus the run's verified claims.

For each distinct value in the array, MongoDB creates a separate entry in the index, and each entry points back to the same document. As a result, a single document can have multiple entries in a multikey index. If an array contains multiple instances of the same value, the index only includes one entry for the value.
